docs.text: SUSE Telco Cloud 3.7 Northline Rancher Prime • Cluster API • Metal3 • Edge Virtualization Start the lab → Quick reference

docs.title: The operator
docs.text:
Northline is a regional mobile network. One management cluster covers the region. Each site is a downstream cluster: a central office, site-co-01, then a far-edge site, site-ran-01.

You prove four things, in order. The management cluster is already running Rancher Prime, Turtles, Cluster API, and Metal3. A downstream cluster is a set of Cluster API objects, bound by Metal3 to hosts that expose Redfish virtual media, then imported by Rancher. A second site is the same shape again. On site-co-01 only, a pod and a KubeVirt VM run side by side.

The EC2 box, when you use AWS, is the KVM host rodeo rented. Metal3 did not create that instance. Every server Metal3 touches is a libvirt guest with a sushy-tools Redfish BMC. There is no Cluster API Provider AWS in this stack.

docs.title: Lab network
docs.text:
KVM host
libvirt network default (virbr0), 192.168.122.0/24
│
├── mgmt       192.168.122.10  management cluster, image cache, Ironic
├── site-co    192.168.122.21  ┐
├── site-co-2  192.168.122.23  ├ hosts for site-co-01 (cluster endpoint .20), nested virt for lab 07
├── site-co-3  192.168.122.24  ┘
└── site-ran   192.168.122.32  host for site-ran-01 (cluster endpoint .22)
VM Role Start size, not a measured pin mgmt Management cluster, image cache, Ironic 8 vCPU, 16 GB site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3 The three hosts of site-co-01, KubeVirt in lab 07 4 vCPU, 8 GB each, nested virt site-ran The host of site-ran-01 4 vCPU, 8 GB

rodeo up stops when those hosts are available. You apply the downstream Cluster yourself. rodeo does not apply manifests/.

Each VM gets a fixed DHCP reservation on 192.168.122.0/24, libvirt network default, bridge virbr0. Read each address with virsh domifaddr.

docs.title: Two ways to start
docs.text:
AWS first. Bare metal second. The labs are the same pages. The split is where the KVM host comes from.

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avaleror/rodeo-cli/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --ref v0.28.1
git clone https://github.com/avaleror/suse-telco-workshop.git
cd suse-telco-workshop
rodeo doctor
rodeo up                  # bare metal host
# AWS: rodeo up --target aws

v0.28.1 (9f616b6) has the five-VM layout as its built-in default. v0.27.0 was the first rodeo-cli release with type: suse-telco. Check the hardware requirements first. Details are in the README and host setup.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
Exercise 01 Tour the region 20 min Find Rancher, the libvirt hosts, sushy, and the image cache. Read the versions. Exercise 02 Management stack 20 min Identify Rancher Prime, Turtles, Cluster API, the RKE2 providers, Metal3, and Ironic. No install. Exercise 03 Enroll site servers 25 min Read the BareMetalHost objects, the redfish-virtualmedia URL, and state available. Exercise 04 First downstream cluster 40 min Apply the three-node manifest for site-co-01 and watch Turtles import it. Exercise 05 Clusters at scale 30 min Apply the ClusterClass and site-ran-01. Both clusters show in one Rancher. Exercise 06 Site console 20 min Fleet delivers the operations console on NodePort 30080. Operator language calls this the CNF-side workload. Exercise 07 Edge Virtualization 40 min On site-co-01 only, start one KubeVirt guest next to the console pod.

Times are writing targets, not a measured run.

docs.title: SUSE Telco Cloud 3.7: Lab guide
docs.text:
Version: 3.7 | Date: 3 October 2026 | Duration: about 3 hours 15 minutes, as a writing target Author: Andres Valero, Principal Technology Advocate, SUSE

This is the print rollup of labs 01 through 07. The short pages under Exercises are the same labs with a next link.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Northline is a regional mobile network. One management cluster covers the region. Your job is to see two downstream clusters in Rancher Prime, then one pod and one KubeVirt guest on site-co-01.

This guide uses the product names (edition: product). With edition: opensource read Rancher for Rancher Prime and openSUSE Leap Micro 6.2 for SUSE Linux Micro 6.2; everything else is the same.

The KVM host is already up when class starts. libvirt network default, bridge virbr0, subnet 192.168.122.0/24. VMs: mgmt (.10), site-co (.21), site-co-2 (.23), site-co-3 (.24), site-ran (.32). The admin password is in ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml.

manifests/ is the student YAML, and rodeo does not apply it. Lab 04 applies site-co-01, lab 05 applies ClusterClass example-clusterclass and site-ran-01, and lab 07 applies VirtualMachine site-co-guest on site-co-01.

Words: say downstream cluster or runtime stack. Say Edge Virtualization for the feature and KubeVirt for the project. When a sentence says CNF or VNF, it is operator language. The full list is Product language.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
VM Role Start size mgmt Management cluster, image cache, Ironic, Gitea 8 vCPU, 16 GB site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3 Hosts for site-co-01, nested virt 4 vCPU, 8 GB each site-ran Host for site-ran-01 4 vCPU, 8 GB

AWS callout: EC2 is the KVM host rodeo rented. Metal3 did not create it. Bare metal callout: this machine is the KVM host, and the BMCs are still sushy-tools.

docs.title: Lab 1: Tour the region (20 min)
docs.text:
virsh list --all
virsh domifaddr mgmt
virsh domifaddr site-co
virsh domifaddr site-co-2
virsh domifaddr site-co-3
virsh domifaddr site-ran

Open a shell on mgmt as root (ssh root@192.168.122.10 from the KVM host, as root) and fetch the workshop files there. Every kubectl and helm command from here on runs in that shell, from that directory:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/avaleror/suse-telco-workshop/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz | tar xz
cd suse-telco-workshop-main
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl version

Find Rancher, the five guests, sushy, and the image cache. Read the versions on the landing page.

docs.title: Lab 2: Management stack (20 min)
docs.text:
No install. rodeo up already installed Rancher Prime, Turtles, Cluster API, the RKE2 providers, Metal3, and Ironic.

kubectl get pods -A
kubectl api-resources | grep -Ei 'cluster|metal3|baremetal|turtles|rke2'

docs.title: Lab 3: Enroll site servers (25 min)
docs.text:
kubectl get baremetalhosts -A -o yaml

All four hosts are available. The BMC URL uses redfish-virtualmedia. A real server keeps the API and changes the address.

docs.title: Lab 4: First downstream cluster (40 min)
docs.text:
Apply manifests/site-co.yaml for site-co-01. The file sets cloudProviderEnabled: false, RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1, Cilium, and cluster-api.cattle.io/rancher-auto-import: "true". Three control-plane replicas, one per site-co host. No workers. No networkData on Metal3DataTemplate. Endpoint 192.168.122.20, a MetalLB address. Host labels cluster-role: control-plane and site: site-co. Its files block ships MetalLB, endpoint-copier and SUSE Storage (three replicas) with the cluster.

kubectl apply -f manifests/site-co.yaml
kubectl get clusters -A
kubectl get machines -n default

Watch Turtles import site-co-01. To start over, delete only the Cluster: kubectl delete cluster -n default site-co-01. Deleting the whole file hangs the RKE2 control plane deletion.

docs.title: Lab 5: Clusters at scale (30 min)
docs.text:
Apply ClusterClass example-clusterclass in namespace northline, then site-ran-01. One host, endpoint 192.168.122.22 (a MetalLB address, the host is .32), host labels deploy-region: northline and cluster-type: site-ran. Both clusters show in one Rancher. The lab stops at two sites. The Rancher Manager 2.15 large row is the published ceiling to quote: 500 clusters and 5,000 nodes, at 16 vCPU and 64 GB per management node, under that page's assumptions.

kubectl apply -f manifests/clusterclass.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/site-ran.yaml
kubectl get clusters -A

Production RAN sites run the SUSE Linux Micro real-time image on tuned bare metal. This lab uses the standard image: the sites are nested VMs.

docs.title: Lab 6: Site console (20 min)
docs.text:
Label both sites demo=true and site-type=downstream, then apply manifests/site-console-gitrepo.yaml. NodePort 30080. The pod is an operations console. Operator language: CNF-side workload.

kubectl get clusters.fleet.cattle.io -n fleet-default -L demo,site-type
kubectl get gitrepo -n fleet-default
kubectl get bundle -A

Check Bundle status. CLUSTER_NAME matches site-co-01 or site-ran-01.

docs.title: Lab 7: Edge Virtualization (40 min)
docs.text:
On site-co-01 only. KubeVirt 1.8.3 and CDI 1.65.0 (both chart 307.0.3+up0.8.0), dashboard extension 1.4.2 (chart 307.0.5+up1.4.2). SUSE Storage 1.12.1 is already the default class, three replicas, installed with the cluster in lab 4. Then apply VirtualMachine site-co-guest. CDI imports the disk. Guide language: Edge Virtualization. Operator language: the VM is a VNF.

kubectl get secret -n default site-co-01-kubeconfig -o jsonpath='{.data.value}' | base64 -d > ~/site-co-01.kubeconfig
export KUBECONFIG=~/site-co-01.kubeconfig
kubectl apply -f manifests/kubevirt-vm.yaml
kubectl get vm,vmi

Open the console and the VM. Both are running on site-co-01.

docs.title: After the labs
docs.text: Bonus, not numbered points at real Redfish, dhcp-less nmstate, SR-IOV, CPU Manager, and the air-gap ISO. Those are not required to finish the class.

docs.title: Exercise 1: Tour the region
docs.text:
Time: 20 min Next: Exercise 2: Management stack

AWS

The EC2 instance is the KVM host. rodeo rented it. Metal3 did not create that instance. Every server Metal3 enrolls is a libvirt guest with a sushy-tools Redfish BMC. There is no Cluster API Provider AWS in this stack.

Bare metal

This machine is the KVM host. The BMCs are still sushy-tools. A later track points the same YAML at a server's Redfish virtual-media address.

Get your bearings before you apply anything. The lab network is libvirt network default, bridge virbr0, subnet 192.168.122.0/24. The VM names are mgmt, site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3, and site-ran.

virsh list --all
virsh domifaddr mgmt
virsh domifaddr site-co
virsh domifaddr site-co-2
virsh domifaddr site-co-3
virsh domifaddr site-ran

rodeo up should already show mgmt running, with the four site hosts present as the machines Metal3 will enroll: three for site-co-01 and one for site-ran-01. Read the Rancher URL from the success screen. The admin password is in ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml on the KVM host. Rancher uses its own self-signed certificate (rancher_tls.source: rancher), on a NodePort. You do not need a public listener on port 80 or 443.

docs.title: Your shell on mgmt
docs.text:
Every kubectl and helm command in labs 01 through 07 runs on the management VM, mgmt, as root. rodeo installed both there and gave root a kubeconfig for the management cluster, so there is nothing to configure.

From the KVM host, as root (run sudo -i first if you logged in as another user):

ssh root@192.168.122.10

Then fetch the workshop files on mgmt and work from that directory for the rest of the class:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/avaleror/suse-telco-workshop/archive/refs/heads/main.tar.gz | tar xz
cd suse-telco-workshop-main
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl version

virsh commands, like the ones above, run on the KVM host, not on mgmt. Keep a second terminal on the host for them.

Read the versions from kubectl version against the landing page table.

Then find the image cache on mgmt. It is nginx in namespace imagecache, serving /opt/media at http://imagecache.local:8080. It already holds eibimage-downstream-cluster.raw and its .sha256, built before class with Edge Image Builder edge-image-builder:1.3.4, so you are not waiting on a build.

kubectl -n imagecache get pods
ls -lh /opt/media

Open Rancher and confirm you are looking at one management cluster for the region. The downstream clusters are not there yet. You create those in labs 04 and 05.

Next: Exercise 2: Management stack

docs.title: Exercise 2: Management stack
docs.text:
Time: 20 min Next: Exercise 3: Enroll site servers

rodeo up already installed the management stack. This lab is identification, not an install.

In Rancher, and with kubectl in your shell on mgmt, find each of these:

  • Rancher Prime 2.15.1
  • Rancher Turtles v0.27.1, built into Rancher, plus the providers chart 307.0.8+up0.27.0
  • Cluster API controller v1.13.3
  • The RKE2 bootstrap and control-plane providers, v0.25.0
  • CAPM3 v1.13.2
  • Metal3, chart 307.0.31+up0.16.0, with baremetal-operator 0.13.3
  • Ironic 38.0.0
  • cert-manager 1.20.1
kubectl get pods -A
kubectl api-resources | grep -Ei 'cluster|metal3|baremetal|turtles|rke2'

Open source edition

With edition: opensource you see Rancher 2.15.1 from the community chart instead of Rancher Prime, and the node OS is openSUSE Leap Micro 6.2. Every other component and version on this page is the same.

The management node is RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1 on SUSE Linux Micro 6.2. Cilium is the CNI on that image. Ironic keeps its working data on an emptyDir volume, the Metal3 chart default for a single management node. SUSE Storage is not installed on mgmt.

You should see the controllers the platform waits for: Cluster API, CAPM3, IPAM CRDs, the RKE2 providers, cert-manager, baremetal-operator, Ironic, and Turtles. IPAM CRDs can be present. This lab does not use upstream Metal3 IPAM objects.

NeuVector is not part of this lab. If you do not see it, that is the pin.

Next: Exercise 3: Enroll site servers

docs.title: Exercise 3: Enroll site servers
docs.text:
Time: 25 min Next: Exercise 4: First downstream cluster

rodeo up registers four BareMetalHost objects and waits until they are available. You do not enroll them by hand. You read the objects and see what a real server would change.

kubectl get baremetalhosts -A
kubectl get baremetalhosts -A -o yaml

Check three fields on each host:

  1. State is available.
  2. The BMC address is a redfish-virtualmedia URL. That method is the only supported BMC method in this stack.
  3. Three hosts carry the labels cluster-role: control-plane and site: site-co: site-co, site-co-2 and site-co-3. The fourth, site-ran, lives in namespace northline. All four sit on libvirt network default, subnet 192.168.122.0/24. The BMC is sushy-tools on the KVM host.

A real server uses this same API. The BMC URL changes from sushy-tools to that server's Redfish virtual-media address. The student YAML stays the telco-examples shape. That hardware track is not this lab.

Three hosts for the central office and one for the far edge. Every node is a control-plane node. There is no worker pool in v1.

Next: Exercise 4: First downstream cluster

docs.title: Exercise 4: First downstream cluster
docs.text:
Time: 40 min Next: Exercise 5: Clusters at scale

This lab creates site-co-01, the central office. It is a downstream cluster, also called the runtime stack. It has three control-plane nodes, one on each of site-co, site-co-2 and site-co-3, and no workers. Three nodes is what a central office runs: the cluster keeps working if one host fails.

manifests/site-co.yaml is the 3.7 Metal3 quickstart set from telco-examples release-3.7 (e4ec0b0), DHCP tree, with SR-IOV charts removed. The file already sets cloudProviderEnabled: false, RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1, Cilium, and this label:

cluster-api.cattle.io/rancher-auto-import: "true"

The Metal3DataTemplate carries metaData only. There is no networkData and no upstream IPAM. The machine template selects hosts labeled cluster-role: control-plane and site: site-co, and three hosts match.

A three-node cluster cannot use one host's address for its API. The control plane endpoint is 192.168.122.20, a MetalLB address. The files block in the same file writes Helm charts and objects into /var/lib/rancher/rke2/server/manifests/ on every node, and RKE2 applies them on first boot:

  • MetalLB and endpoint-copier-operator, which announce 192.168.122.20 and keep the kubernetes-vip Service pointed at the API servers
  • SUSE Storage 1.12.1, three replicas, so the cluster comes up with a default storage class

This is the layout in the SUSE Telco Cloud 3.7 guide, Downstream cluster provisioning with Directed network provisioning (multi-node), with MetalLB as the load balancer. As in that chapter, RKE2ControlPlane sets registrationAddress to the VIP and carries the load-balancer-exclusion annotation, so MetalLB stops sending API traffic to a node while Cluster API drains it. The guide's second MetalLB pool, for Traefik ingress, is left out: the labs reach the sites on NodePorts. site-ran-01 gets the same MetalLB pattern from its ClusterClass in lab 05.

In your shell on mgmt, from the suse-telco-workshop-main directory (lab 01), apply it and watch Turtles import the cluster:

kubectl apply -f manifests/site-co.yaml
kubectl get clusters -A
kubectl get machines -n default

Cluster API adds the nodes one at a time. The cluster turns Available after the first node, and the other two follow. Wait until all three machines are Running.

In Rancher, site-co-01 should show up because of the auto-import label. This workshop teaches that path only: provisioned by Cluster API plus Metal3, then imported by Rancher Turtles.

The hosts are site-co, site-co-2 and site-co-3. Lab 07 needs nested virt on them. You do not start the VM in this lab.

Starting over

Delete the Cluster object only: kubectl delete cluster -n default site-co-01. Cluster API removes the machines and releases the host. kubectl delete -f manifests/site-co.yaml also deletes the Metal3MachineTemplate while the cluster is still going away, and the RKE2 control plane deletion hangs.

Next: Exercise 5: Clusters at scale

docs.title: Exercise 5: Clusters at scale
docs.text:
Time: 30 min Next: Exercise 6: Site console

site-co-01 is already up from lab 04, written out object by object. A far-edge site is smaller and there are many of them, so an operator stamps them out from a template instead. ClusterClass example-clusterclass in namespace northline is that template. This lab adds site-ran-01, one host. Run it in your shell on mgmt, from the suse-telco-workshop-main directory.

kubectl apply -f manifests/clusterclass.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/site-ran.yaml
kubectl get clusters -A

manifests/clusterclass.yaml creates the namespace and example-clusterclass. manifests/site-ran.yaml creates site-ran-01 from that class, one control-plane replica, RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1, the auto-import label, and endpoint 192.168.122.22. That endpoint is a MetalLB address on the new cluster, not the address of the site-ran host, which is 192.168.122.32. The class owns the control-plane machine template. Cluster API clones it for each cluster and fills in the site type, so site-ran-01 selects cluster-role: control-plane, deploy-region: northline, and cluster-type: site-ran from the variable clusterType: site-ran.

Both clusters should show in the same Rancher. site-ran-01 is the far-edge site. It does not get KubeVirt.

Real-time kernel

In production, RAN sites run the SUSE Linux Micro real-time image on tuned bare metal. This lab uses the standard image for every site: the sites are nested VMs, so a real-time kernel would show nothing here.

Scale, as this lab teaches it, is a replica count plus one BareMetalHost per machine. The lab stops at two sites.

The talk track uses the Rancher Manager 2.15 large row as the published ceiling: 500 clusters and 5,000 nodes, at 16 vCPU and 64 GB per management node, under the assumptions on that page. The Telco Cloud guide does not publish a downstream count of its own. More than one management cluster is how you cover regions and limit upgrade blast radius. Northline uses one.

Next: Exercise 6: Site console

docs.title: Exercise 6: Site console
docs.text:
Time: 20 min Next: Exercise 7: Edge Virtualization

The container on the site is an operations console. Operator language: this is the CNF-side workload. The pod is still an operations console. It has no user plane, no SR-IOV, and no Multus.

Fleet delivers it. The GitRepo targets clusters labelled demo=true and site-type=downstream. Selectors inside the console fleet.yaml do not apply when the GitRepo sets its own targets. Do not go looking for a bank=true label.

docs.title: Label the sites
docs.text:
The imported clusters carry no labels yet. Fleet reads them from the Rancher cluster objects, and those have generated IDs (c-xxxxx), so look each one up by its display name. Run this in your shell on mgmt. You can also add the labels in the Rancher UI, under Cluster Management, Edit Config.

for c in site-co-01 site-ran-01; do
  id=$(kubectl get clusters.management.cattle.io \
    -o jsonpath="{.items[?(@.spec.displayName==\"$c\")].metadata.name}")
  kubectl label clusters.management.cattle.io "$id" demo=true site-type=downstream --overwrite
done
kubectl get clusters.fleet.cattle.io -n fleet-default -L demo,site-type

Both sites should show true and downstream. Rancher copies the labels to the Fleet clusters within a few seconds.

docs.title: Deliver the console
docs.text:
kubectl apply -f manifests/site-console-gitrepo.yaml
kubectl get gitrepo -n fleet-default
kubectl get bundle -n fleet-default

The GitRepo points at Gitea on mgmt: http://192.168.122.10:3000/gitea/telco-site-console.git. rodeo copied https://github.com/avaleror/telco-site-console.git, the fleet_repo value in rodeo-plan.yaml, into that Gitea when it built the lab. Fleet never goes to GitHub. You can browse the repo at http://192.168.122.10:3000/gitea/telco-site-console from the KVM host.

The console shows its own site name in the header. Rancher labels each Fleet cluster with its display name, and the repo's fleet.yaml passes that label to the chart.

When the bundle is ready, open the console on node port 30080 of a host in each site: 192.168.122.21 (or .23, .24) for site-co-01, 192.168.122.32 for site-ran-01. CLUSTER_NAME in the console must match the cluster you are on. Check Bundle status, not only the NodePort. A console can answer on 30080 while the bundle is NotReady, for example when one image in the repo fails to pull. A LoadBalancer Service with no provider left a previous workshop Bundle NotReady. That Service stays out of the bundle.

Live panels are cluster facts. Simulated rows stay labeled simulated.

Next: Exercise 7: Edge Virtualization

docs.title: Exercise 7: Edge Virtualization
docs.text:
Time: 40 min Next: Lab overview

Do this on site-co-01 only. site-ran-01 stays without a guest. The guest in manifests/kubevirt-vm.yaml is VirtualMachine site-co-guest.

Guide language: Edge Virtualization. The project is KubeVirt. Operator language: the VM is a VNF. It is one guest. Harvester is out of scope.

Every command in this lab goes to site-co-01, not to the management cluster. Cluster API keeps the cluster's kubeconfig in a Secret on mgmt. In your shell on mgmt, from the suse-telco-workshop-main directory, write it to a file and point kubectl and helm at it:

kubectl get secret -n default site-co-01-kubeconfig -o jsonpath='{.data.value}' | base64 -d > ~/site-co-01.kubeconfig
export KUBECONFIG=~/site-co-01.kubeconfig
kubectl get nodes

Three nodes, all Ready. The API address in that file is https://192.168.122.20:6443, the MetalLB address from lab 04. To go back to the management cluster, run unset KUBECONFIG.

docs.title: Storage is already there
docs.text:
The guest disk is a PersistentVolumeClaim, so site-co-01 needs a storage class before CDI can import anything. SUSE Storage 1.12.1 (Longhorn) came with the cluster in lab 04: the files block in manifests/site-co.yaml installed it on first boot. Check it:

kubectl get storageclass
kubectl -n longhorn-system get nodes.longhorn.io

longhorn is the default class, and all three nodes show in SUSE Storage. The class keeps three replicas of every volume, one per node, so a volume survives the loss of one host. SUSE Storage needs open-iscsi and a running iscsid on every node. The site image rodeo builds already has both. If the Longhorn pods never get Ready, check iscsid on the site-co hosts first.

docs.title: KubeVirt and CDI
docs.text:
Install KubeVirt and CDI from the SUSE registry at the pins in rodeo-plan.yaml:

  • KubeVirt 1.8.3, chart 307.0.3+up0.8.0
  • CDI 1.65.0, chart 307.0.3+up0.8.0
  • dashboard extension 1.4.2, chart 307.0.5+up1.4.2
helm install kubevirt oci://registry.suse.com/edge/charts/kubevirt \
  --version 307.0.3+up0.8.0 -n kubevirt-system --create-namespace
helm install cdi oci://registry.suse.com/edge/charts/cdi \
  --version 307.0.3+up0.8.0 -n cdi-system --create-namespace
kubectl -n kubevirt-system wait kubevirt --all --for=condition=Available --timeout=600s
kubectl -n cdi-system wait cdi --all --for=condition=Available --timeout=300s

The Edge Virtualization chapter has the dashboard extension steps. CDI imports the disk. Longhorn V2 backing images are not supported for this import.

docs.title: The guest
docs.text:
site-co needs nested virt or the guest will not start. On AWS, m8id.4xlarge passed this lab: the guest ran with KVM acceleration, not emulation. No metal size is needed.

That file is the guest only. It does not install KubeVirt or Harvester. CDI imports the disk from the registry source in the manifest onto the default storage class.

kubectl apply -f manifests/kubevirt-vm.yaml
kubectl get dv,pvc
kubectl get vm,vmi
kubectl get pods -A | grep -E 'virt|site-console|console'

The DataVolume reaches Succeeded first, then the VMI goes Running. Open the console pod and site-co-guest. Both should be running on site-co-01.

Next: Bonus, not numbered

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text:
Northline is a regional mobile network, a telecom operator (CSP in the industry phrase). One management cluster covers the region. Students use the same labs 01 through 07 on AWS and on bare metal. You only change where the KVM host comes from.

SUSE Telco Cloud 3.7.0 support window, for your planning: full support ends 22 March 2027, maintenance ends 22 March 2028, end of life 23 March 2028.

docs.title: Shared facts
docs.text:
Item Value Plan type: suse-telco, deployment_target: baremetal AWS command rodeo up --target aws from this same repo Network libvirt default, bridge virbr0, 192.168.122.0/24 VMs mgmt, site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3, site-ran (declared in definition.yaml) Hardware x86_64 with VT-x or AMD-V and nested virt on, 24 threads, 64 GB RAM, 350 GB SSD or NVMe. Details: Architecture and hardware Rancher TLS source: rancher (self-signed), NodePort, no public 80/443 Secrets ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml only

deployment_target: aws on the instance raises disk floors and can use NVMe for images. Fleet workshop files, if any, keep lab.target: baremetal. Do not set lab.target: aws.

rodeo up --target aws overrides a committed deployment_target: baremetal and writes aws back into the local plan. One plan file is enough. The EC2 host is seeded from the copy bundled in rodeo-cli, which is kept identical to this repo's plan.

docs.title: AWS
docs.text:
rodeo up --target aws rents an EC2 instance and uses it as the KVM host. Libvirt guests on that instance are the lab machines. sushy-tools on the host is their BMC. Metal3 enrolls those guests. The EC2 API is not on that path.

Say this to the room: the EC2 box was rented by rodeo, and every server Metal3 touched was a libvirt guest with a fake Redfish BMC. There is no Cluster API Provider AWS in the Telco Cloud stack.

Tested size: m8id.4xlarge (16 threads, 64 GiB) in eu-north-1 ran labs 01 through 07 with both editions, opensource on 2026-11-10 and product on 2026-11-11. The five-VM layout, with site-co-01 on three hosts and SUSE Storage built in, passed on the same size on 2026-11-11 with the product edition. Nested KubeVirt worked on that virtual instance: the lab 07 guest ran with KVM acceleration. No metal size is needed.

Credentials stay in ~/.aws/credentials or the environment. Do not put them in rodeo-plan.yaml.

Tear-down is rodeo destroy --cloud or rodeo fleet deprovision.

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
deployment_target: baremetal means the machine under rodeo is the KVM host. No cloud provider: block.

This first slice uses the same libvirt guests and the same sushy-tools BMC as AWS. Tell the room that. An operator will picture a rack, and this slice is still a KVM host with emulated BMCs.

Real Redfish hardware is a later track. The student YAML stays the telco-examples shape. The BMC URL changes from sushy-tools to the server's Redfish virtual-media address.

Tear-down is sudo rodeo clean --yes.

docs.title: Choose the edition
docs.text:
edition in rodeo-plan.yaml decides what the lab is built from. The Telco Cloud 3.7 pins, the charts, the labs and the student YAML are the same in both.

product (default) opensource Host OS for mgmt and the sites SUSE Linux Micro 6.2 openSUSE Leap Micro 6.2 Rancher Rancher Prime 2.15.1 Rancher 2.15.1, community chart Base image you stage it once (SUSE login) rodeo downloads it, checksum pinned SCC registration code optional not used

Neither edition needs an SCC code. The packages added to the downstream image are jq and open-iscsi (SUSE Storage needs it in lab 07), and Edge Image Builder installs them from a public repository: SLE BCI 16.0 for product, openSUSE Leap 16.0 for opensource. In product, an scc_registration_code in ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml (and uncommented in the plan) switches that to SUSE's own repositories.

docs.title: Stage the SL Micro base image (product only)
docs.text:
The mgmt VM and the downstream image both start from SL-Micro.x86_64-6.2-Base-GM.raw.xz. It is only on the SUSE Linux Micro download page, behind a SUSE login, so rodeo cannot fetch it for you. Download it once and copy it to the KVM host before rodeo up:

sudo cp SL-Micro.x86_64-6.2-Base-GM.raw.xz /var/lib/libvirt/images/

Or set telco.base_image.url in rodeo-plan.yaml to a location the host can fetch, and telco.base_image.sha256 to have rodeo check it. The opensource edition skips this step.

On --target aws the copy does not work: rodeo creates the instance in the same run, and it mounts the instance NVMe over /var/lib/libvirt/images. Use telco.base_image.url there, with a URL the instance can fetch, for example a presigned link to a private S3 object in the same region. Do not publish the image: it is SUSE content behind a login.

docs.title: Install rodeo-cli
docs.text:
install.sh on main tracks main. Pin the tag this README names:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avaleror/rodeo-cli/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --ref v0.28.1

v0.28.1 is commit 9f616b6 (11 November 2026). Its engine code is the same as v0.27.0 (0da19e3), the first release with type: suse-telco, which passed the full lab run with both editions. v0.28.0 made the five-VM layout the built-in default, and that layout passed on 2026-11-11. v0.28.1 only fixes a crash when a plan has an empty telco: block. Replace that ref only after a full lab run names the commit you actually tested.

git clone https://github.com/avaleror/suse-telco-workshop.git
cd suse-telco-workshop
rodeo doctor
rodeo up                  # bare metal
# AWS: rodeo up --target aws

Because this directory already has rodeo-plan.yaml, rodeo up is meant to skip rodeo init, write ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml, and wrap the deploy so a dropped SSH session does not kill it.

rodeo up is done when both BareMetalHost objects are available. Students apply manifests/ after that. rodeo does not apply that directory.

docs.title: After the first boot
docs.text: Raise the mgmt VM if Ironic or Rancher starve. The 8 vCPU and 16 GB figures are a start, not a measured pin. SUSE Storage is not installed on mgmt: on a single node, Ironic's volume is an emptyDir, the Metal3 chart default. NeuVector stays out.

docs.title: Pre-lab checklist
docs.text: Run this after rodeo up finishes and before students open lab 01.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
test -f ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml && echo secrets file present
# Passwords resolve from ?? keys. Nothing secret belongs in rodeo-plan.yaml.
grep -E 'rancher_admin_password|bmc_password|mgmt_root_password' ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml >/dev/null

No SCC registration code is needed. AWS credentials, if you used --target aws, stay in ~/.aws/credentials or the environment.

docs.title: Image cache
docs.text:
On mgmt, the downstream image is already in the cache. Students must not be waiting on Edge Image Builder (edge-image-builder:1.3.4, from rodeo-plan.yaml).

ssh root@MGMT_IP "ls -lh /opt/media && curl -sfI http://imagecache.local:8080/eibimage-downstream-cluster.raw"

Both eibimage-downstream-cluster.raw and eibimage-downstream-cluster.raw.sha256 are there, and the curl returns 200.

docs.title: Controller rollout
docs.text:
On the management cluster, these are ready: Cluster API, CAPM3, IPAM CRDs, RKE2 bootstrap, RKE2 control plane, cert-manager, baremetal-operator, Ironic, and Turtles.

virsh domifaddr mgmt
ssh root@MGMT_IP "kubectl get pods -A"
ssh root@MGMT_IP "kubectl get nodes"

Rancher Prime (product) or Rancher (opensource) should be 2.15.1. The node OS is SUSE Linux Micro 6.2 (product) or openSUSE Leap Micro 6.2 (opensource), RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1.

docs.title: BareMetalHost available
docs.text:
ssh root@MGMT_IP "kubectl get baremetalhosts -A"

Four hosts, all available, BMC method redfish-virtualmedia, sushy-tools addresses: site-co, site-co-2 and site-co-3 in default, site-ran in northline.

docs.title: Nested virt on the site-co hosts
docs.text:
Lab 07 starts a KubeVirt guest on site-co-01, and it can land on any of its three hosts. That guest needs nested virt. site-ran does not.

On the KVM host, nested virt must be on, and the site-co hosts must pass the host CPU through:

cat /sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/nested    # Y (kvm_amd on AMD hosts)
for vm in site-co site-co-2 site-co-3; do virsh dumpxml $vm | grep "cpu mode"; done   # host-passthrough

docs.title: Hand-off
docs.text: Students start at lab 01. Labs 04 through 07 apply the YAML in manifests/: site-co-01, ClusterClass example-clusterclass, site-ran-01, GitRepo telco-site-console, and VirtualMachine site-co-guest.

docs.title: Architecture and hardware
docs.text:
The whole lab runs on nested virtualization on one KVM host. rodeo builds five VMs on that host and gives them a fake Redfish BMC, so Metal3 treats them as bare-metal servers. The lab 07 guest runs one level deeper, inside one of the three site-co hosts.

L0 KVM host · your x86_64 server · SLES 16 or openSUSE Leap 16 1 KVM + libvirtVM disks on local SSD or NVMe Edge Image Builderbuilds the site OS image,copies it to mgmt :8080 2 sushy-tools Redfish BMC192.168.122.1:8000 · podman rodeoruns the build and the tear-down virbr0 · 192.168.122.0/24 · NAT out via .1 virtual media + power L1 mgmt · 192.168.122.10 VM · 8 vCPU · 16 GB · SL Micro 6.2 · single-node RKE2 Metal3baremetal-operator + Ironic Image cache :8080imagecache.local · serves the EIB image Rancher Prime 2.15.1UI on NodePort 30002 Rancher Turtles + Cluster APIRKE2 providers · imports new clusters into Rancher FleetGitRepo telco-site-console · labelled sites Gitea :3000copy of github.com/avaleror/telco-site-console MetalLB · cert-managersupporting charts BareMetalHosts for the four site hosts registered by rodeo · available before lab 04 No SUSE Storage on mgmt. Ironic keeps its data on an emptyDir, the single-node default. Redfish API 3 OS image 4 import bundle 5 L1 site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3 3 VMs · .21 .23 .24 · 4 vCPU · 8 GB each · nested virt site-co-01 · 3-node RKE2 cluster lab 04 · API on VIP .20 (MetalLB) Site console podNodePort 30080 · lab 06 SUSE Storage 1.12.13 replicas · comes with the cluster KubeVirt + CDIlab 07 L2 6 site-co-guest KubeVirt VM with KVM acceleration disk on SUSE Storage, 3 replicas A VM inside a VM on your KVM host listed in the site-co-01 console For lab 07, every site-co host needs /dev/kvm: nested virt on the host and CPU mode host-passthrough on these VMs. L1 site-ran · .32 VM · 4 vCPU · 8 GB site-ran-01 · RKE2 lab 05 · from the ClusterClass Site console podNodePort 30080 · lab 06 API endpoint .22MetalLB address, not the host No KubeVirtfar-edge RAN site Built the same way as site-co: steps 3 to 5 repeat for this VM, with a single node.

Dashed orange lines: Metal3 drives the machines through the Redfish BMC. Solid green lines: images, imports and workloads. The numbers match the steps below.

docs.title: What happens, in order
docs.text:
1. rodeo up, host. rodeo installs KVM and libvirt, creates the five VMs from definition.yaml on virbr0, and starts sushy-tools as the BMC for the four site hosts.
  2. rodeo up, mgmt. mgmt boots SL Micro and gets RKE2, Rancher Prime, Turtles, Cluster API, Metal3, Gitea and the image cache. Edge Image Builder builds the site OS image on the host, and rodeo copies it to imagecache.local:8080.
  3. rodeo up, enroll. rodeo registers four BareMetalHosts at redfish-virtualmedia://192.168.122.1:8000, one per site host, labelled by rodeo's built-in site map (telco.sites in rodeo-plan.yaml overrides it). Ironic inspects each VM through the BMC and marks it available. rodeo stops here, and the students take over.
  4. Labs 04 and 05. kubectl apply creates the Cluster API objects. Metal3 picks hosts by their labels, three for site-co-01 and one for site-ran-01, and Ironic boots its agent on each VM through BMC virtual media. The agent writes the OS image from :8080 to the VM's disk and RKE2 starts. On the first boot RKE2 also installs what the manifests ship with each cluster: MetalLB for the API address (.20 and .22) and, on site-co-01, SUSE Storage. Turtles imports each cluster into Rancher.
  5. Lab 06. Students label both clusters. Fleet clones the console repo from Gitea on mgmt and deploys it to each labelled site on NodePort 30080.
  6. Lab 07. On site-co-01 only, students install KubeVirt and CDI on top of the SUSE Storage the cluster came with. site-co-guest then starts on one of the three hosts, one nesting level below it, with its disk replicated across all three.

docs.title: Nesting depth
docs.text:
Level What runs there L0 The KVM host: your server L1 mgmt, site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3, site-ran: libvirt VMs L2 site-co-guest: a KubeVirt VM inside site-co

Metal3 only sees a Redfish BMC, so the site VMs look like bare-metal servers to it. Swap sushy-tools for real BMCs and the student YAML stays the same. Only the BMC address changes.

If your KVM host is itself a VM, every level moves down by one. site-co-guest then runs three levels deep, and the hypervisor under your host must pass nested virtualization through to it.

docs.title: Hardware requirements
docs.text:
One machine runs the whole lab. rodeo checks the first four rows before it creates any VM and stops if one fails.

Item Required Recommended Why CPU x86_64 with Intel VT-x or AMD-V, turned on in the firmware 24 or more threads The VMs get 24 vCPU in total: 8 for mgmt and 4 for each of the four site hosts. The labs are tested on 16 threads, so the VMs share CPUs: all labs passed, and lab 04 took about 10 minutes for three nodes. With 24 or more threads they do not share. Fewer than 16 is not tested. Nested virtualization On in the KVM module: kvm_intel nested=Y or kvm_amd nested=1 Same site-co runs the lab 07 KubeVirt guest. rodeo checks this setting but does not turn it on. Memory 48 GiB free when rodeo up starts 64 GB in the machine The VMs take 48 GiB: 16 for mgmt and 8 for each of the four site hosts. The host also needs memory for itself and for the Edge Image Builder run. The labs are tested on 64 GB. Disk 260 GB free in /var/lib/libvirt/images 350 GB or more, SSD or NVMe VM disks are 80 GB for mgmt and 40 GB for each of the four site hosts. rodeo adds 20 GB of headroom. The SL Micro base image, the built site image and the lab 07 guest disk come on top of that. The labs are tested on NVMe. Spinning disks are not tested. Host OS SLES 16 or openSUSE Leap 16 Same rodeo installs KVM, libvirt and podman with zypper. Network Outbound HTTPS, and 192.168.122.0/24 free on the host Unfiltered outbound HTTPS The lab pulls images and charts during the build and the labs. libvirt's default network takes 192.168.122.0/24, so no other interface on the host can use it. Access root or sudo on the host, plus SSH from the students' laptops Same rodeo runs as root. Students reach the lab through the host.

No inbound port other than SSH is needed. Rancher (192.168.122.10:30002), Gitea (:3000) and the site consoles (:30080) sit on the private lab network. Open them from the host, or through an SSH tunnel:

ssh -L 30002:192.168.122.10:30002 user@kvm-host   # then open https://localhost:30002

The labs are tested with unfiltered outbound HTTPS. If your network filters it, these are the hosts the build and the labs are known to use. The list has not been tested on a filtered network, so expect to add to it: registry.suse.com, registry.rancher.com, charts.rancher.com, releases.rancher.com, get.rke2.io, github.com and its download hosts under githubusercontent.com, charts.jetstack.io, charts.longhorn.io, Docker Hub (docker.io, registry-1.docker.io), updates.suse.com and download.opensuse.org.

docs.title: Check a host before rodeo up
docs.text:
grep -c -E 'vmx|svm' /proc/cpuinfo                 # more than 0: VT-x or AMD-V is on
nproc                                             # 24 or more threads recommended
cat /sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/nested 2>/dev/null \
  || cat /sys/module/kvm_amd/parameters/nested     # Y or 1
free -g                                           # 48 GiB or more available
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/libvirt/images && df -h /var/lib/libvirt/images   # 260 GB or more free
ip -4 addr | grep 192.168.122.                    # no output, or only virbr0
grep PRETTY_NAME /etc/os-release                  # SLES 16 or openSUSE Leap 16
rodeo doctor                                      # rodeo's own checks

docs.title: Turn on nested virtualization
docs.text:
Do this with no VMs running. On Intel:

echo "options kvm_intel nested=1" | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/kvm-nested.conf
sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel && sudo modprobe kvm_intel
cat /sys/module/kvm_intel/parameters/nested        # Y

On AMD, use kvm_amd in all three lines. The last command prints 1. If modprobe -r fails because the module is in use, reboot. The file in /etc/modprobe.d/ keeps the setting.

If grep -c -E 'vmx|svm' /proc/cpuinfo prints 0, turn on Intel VT-x or AMD-V (sometimes called SVM) in the server's firmware setup first.

docs.title: Bonus, not numbered
docs.text:
No student steps here. These are pointers for after labs 01 through 07.

The numbered labs stay on Cluster API plus Metal3, one management cluster, emulated BMCs, a three-node and a one-node downstream cluster, the site console, and one KubeVirt guest.

telco-examples on release-3.7 (e4ec0b0) is the place to read:

  • A real Redfish virtual-media URL, in place of sushy-tools
  • The dhcp-less nmstate tree
  • SR-IOV
  • CPU Manager
  • The air-gap management ISO

Two other 3.7 onboarding paths exist besides the one this workshop teaches. One is an Edge Image Builder standalone cluster, then an import into Rancher. The numbered labs do not build that path. They use Cluster API plus Metal3, then the Turtles auto-import label.

Later host targets, after AWS and bare metal both finish a full lab run, are instruqt, gcp, vultr, and hetzner. They are names only.

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
Northline runs one management cluster for the region. Sites are downstream clusters. site-co-01 is the central office. site-ran-01 is the far-edge site.

The diagram of how it all nests, and the hardware it needs, are in Architecture and hardware.

VM Role Start size, not a measured pin mgmt Management cluster, image cache, Ironic. Gitea for the Fleet mirror lives here. 8 vCPU, 16 GB site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3 The three hosts of site-co-01. Nested virt so lab 07 can start a guest. 4 vCPU, 8 GB each site-ran Host for site-ran-01. No KubeVirt. 4 vCPU, 8 GB

One subnet on every lab page: 192.168.122.0/24, libvirt network default, bridge virbr0. Each VM has a fixed DHCP reservation: mgmt 192.168.122.10, site-co 192.168.122.21, site-co-2 192.168.122.23, site-co-3 192.168.122.24, site-ran 192.168.122.32. The cluster API addresses are MetalLB addresses: site-co-01 on .20, site-ran-01 on .22. Read them with virsh domifaddr. There is no node named eib.

docs.title: What rodeo builds
docs.text:
rodeo up builds the platform and stops when the BareMetalHost objects are available. That is the management cluster plus four site hosts. The VMs are declared in definition.yaml in this repo. Which of them become BareMetalHosts, and their labels, is rodeo-cli's built-in suse-telco layout. telco.sites in rodeo-plan.yaml can override it, and this repo does not need to.

The management VM is SUSE Linux Micro 6.2 (openSUSE Leap Micro 6.2 with edition: opensource, and community Rancher instead of Rancher Prime) with RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1, Cilium, cert-manager, Rancher Prime, Metal3 and rancher-turtles-providers. Ironic keeps its data on an emptyDir, the single-node default, so SUSE Storage is not installed there. NeuVector is skipped. The downstream image is built with Edge Image Builder at the 3.7 tag in rodeo-plan.yaml and served from http://imagecache.local:8080 on mgmt. Students do not wait on that build.

Rancher TLS is rancher_tls.source: rancher, the self-signed certificate, on a NodePort. The lab does not need a public listener on port 80 or 443.

docs.title: What you apply
docs.text:
manifests/ is yours. rodeo does not apply it.

File Lab Result site-co.yaml 04 Downstream cluster site-co-01, three nodes, with SUSE Storage clusterclass.yaml 05 ClusterClass example-clusterclass site-ran.yaml 05 Downstream cluster site-ran-01 kubevirt-vm.yaml 07 VirtualMachine site-co-guest on site-co-01

Those files are the 3.7 objects from telco-examples release-3.7 (e4ec0b0), with SR-IOV removed. example-clusterclass and site-ran-01 live in namespace northline. site-co-01 and site-co-guest use default.

docs.title: Hosts
docs.text:
AWS: rodeo up --target aws rents the EC2 instance and uses it as the KVM host. Metal3 never calls the EC2 API. The guests it provisions are libvirt VMs with a sushy-tools BMC.

Bare metal: the Linux machine you are on is already the KVM host. Same guests, same sushy-tools BMC.

Fleet files, if any, keep lab.target: baremetal. Do not set lab.target: aws.

docs.title: Tear-down
docs.text:
AWS: rodeo destroy --cloud or rodeo fleet deprovision. Credentials stay in ~/.aws/credentials or the environment. They do not go in rodeo-plan.yaml.

Bare metal: sudo rodeo clean --yes.

docs.title: Product language
docs.text:
Use these words on the student pages so the lab matches the SUSE Telco Cloud 3.7 guide.

Say this When Downstream cluster, or runtime stack The site cluster. The guide does not say "workload cluster". Management cluster, or management stack The Rancher Prime cluster that owns the sites. Rancher Prime The product. The bill of materials name is SUSE Rancher Prime 2.15.1. The open source edition runs community Rancher 2.15.1. SUSE Linux Micro 6.2 The host OS. ISO names use the SL-Micro prefix. The guide does not tell you to install a product named SLE Micro. Edge Virtualization The feature. KubeVirt The project, at 1.8.3 in this lab. redfish-virtualmedia The only BMC method this stack supports.

Containers are the primary workload in the guide, described as CNFs across Packet Core, RAN, OSS, and BSS. When a page says CNF or VNF, label that sentence as operator language. The pod in lab 06 is an operations console. The VM in lab 07 is one guest.

CSP belongs in the instructor intro, next to the guide's words "telecom operators". Northline is a telecom operator.

Leave these out of the numbered labs:

  • Harvester
  • Cluster API Provider AWS
  • A second management cluster
  • Elemental phone-home as a numbered path
  • K3s as something to install or teach

Elemental phone-home, image-based standalone clusters, and a second management cluster are real 3.7 paths. They are named on the bonus page. They are not labs 01 through 07.

docs.title: Names
docs.text: Item Value Operator Northline Management VM mgmt Site hosts site-co, site-co-2, site-co-3, site-ran Downstream clusters site-co-01, site-ran-01 ClusterClass example-clusterclass in namespace northline Guest VM site-co-guest on site-co-01 Network libvirt default, bridge virbr0 Subnet 192.168.122.0/24 Host addresses mgmt .10, site-co .21, site-co-2 .23, site-co-3 .24, site-ran .32 Cluster endpoints site-co-01 .20, site-ran-01 .22 (MetalLB) DNS domain northline.telco Plan type suse-telco Edition product (default) or opensource Default target baremetal Console NodePort 30080 Fleet labels demo=true, site-type=downstream Auto-import label cluster-api.cattle.io/rancher-auto-import: "true" BMC method redfish-virtualmedia

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
virsh list --all
virsh domifaddr mgmt

rodeo doctor
rodeo up
rodeo up --target aws

kubectl apply -f manifests/site-co.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/clusterclass.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/site-ran.yaml
kubectl apply -f manifests/kubevirt-vm.yaml

Apply the first three files on the management cluster. Apply kubevirt-vm.yaml on site-co-01.

docs.title: Tear-down
docs.text:
# AWS
rodeo destroy --cloud
# or: rodeo fleet deprovision

# Bare metal
sudo rodeo clean --yes

docs.title: Pins
docs.text:
Piece Pin rodeo-cli tag named in the README v0.28.1 (9f616b6) SUSE Telco Cloud 3.7.0 RKE2 v1.36.3+rke2r1 Rancher Prime 2.15.1 Turtles providers chart 307.0.8+up0.27.0 Metal3 chart 307.0.31+up0.16.0 KubeVirt / CDI 1.8.3 / 1.65.0 telco-examples e4ec0b0 on release-3.7

Password: ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml on the KVM host. No SCC code is needed; an optional one (product edition) goes in that file too.
